fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the single access point at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles along its full length to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to pass.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround area near the main residence so drivers of large vehicles can reposition without blocking the drive.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway to maintain overhead and side clearance for large emergency vehicles.
• Thin dense vegetation between the multiple structures so responders can move on foot between buildings without obstruction.
• Post a property map or diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the access drive, and the turnaround area.
• Keep a pedestrian path clear between each detached structure and the main residence.
• Assign and post visible unit or structure identifiers on each detached building so responders can quickly distinguish and communicate about each structure by name or number.
• Keep any gates along the driveway unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box so responders are not delayed at a single point of access.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the lower driveway to give arriving responders an unobstructed view of the structures before reaching

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that extend directly over or touch the roof and walls of the house.
• Thin trees and shrubs on the sides of the house where vegetation grows close to the exterior walls.
• Remove shrubs growing immediately next to the structure to create open space between plants and the building.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the house so individual trees are separated from each other and from the structure.
• Cut grass around the house and outbuildings short, particularly during dry months.
• Clear brush from both sides of the driveway along its full length to keep the travel lane open.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over the driveway to maintain overhead clearance for vehicles.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from inside the brush area closest to the house.
• Thin shrubs within the brush area nearest to the structure so plants are spread apart rather than growing in a continuous mass.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, leaves, and debris that could block access.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the main road.
• Maintain a turnaround area near the house so emergency vehicles can reverse direction on the single access route.
